adds.title: Transgender rights in Canada (Wikipedia; Prisons section)
adds.summary: Wikipedia 'Transgender rights in Canada', Prisons section (accessed 4 Oct 2026): at the federal level the Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) permits gender-diverse offenders to request placement or transfer to a men's or women's institution aligned with their gender identity or expression, regardless of anatomy or the sex marker on their identification documents; requests are assessed individually and may be refused where an unresolved 'overriding health or safety concern' exists under CSC's 2022 gender-diversity policy. The article reports that as of 2025 CSC recorded 90 self-identified transgender women in federal custody - 73 housed in men's institutions and 17 in women's - and that between fiscal years 2017-18 and 2024-25 CSC received 129 placement/transfer requests from people assigned male at birth to women's institutions (35 approved, 72 denied, 22 withdrawn). Provincial correctional policies vary and the article does not document a New Brunswick provincial-jail placement rule; the federal policy is the framework a trans prisoner in federal custody in New Brunswick stands under. The Correctional Investigator has criticised the policy's unclear 'health or safety' override criteria and the lack of a dedicated abuse-reporting mechanism.

records.note: Within budget no New Brunswick-specific trans-prisoner-placement source was found (Wikipedia full-text search surfaced no NB trans-prisoner article; the record's own sources address school policy, not custody). The verified add documents the applicable federal framework: CSC places federal prisoners (incl. those held in federal institutions in New Brunswick) by gender identity on an individual-assessed basis since 2018 (90 trans women in federal custody as of 2025; 73 in men's, 17 in women's institutions; 35 of 129 AMAB women's-institution transfer requests approved 2017/18-2024/25), while NB provincial jail policy is not documented in the sources found. Adds: 1 verified (fetched).

adds.title: LGBTQ people in prison (Wikipedia; Mexico/CDMX section)
adds.summary: Thin: Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ people in prison' article, Mexico section (accessed 4 Oct 2026), documents only one Mexico City prison-system policy: in July 2007, through the efforts of the (capital's) National Human Rights Commission (CDHDF), the Mexico City prison system began allowing same-sex conjugal visits on the basis of a 2003 law banning discrimination based on sexual orientation, with the visitor not required to be married to the inmate and the change applying to all Mexico City prisons. The article contains no data on trans-prisoner housing placement in Mexico City (birth-sex vs identity placement), special units, or segregation practice; the country-level MEX record carries the same finding.

records.note: No trans-specific prison-placement rule or housing practice for Mexico City was found within budget: the Wikipedia full-text search surfaced no CDMX trans-prisoner placement article (only the generic 'LGBTQ people in prison' article and a Mexican prisoners'-rights activist biography), and the verified add is thin - it documents the 2007 CDHDF-led same-sex conjugal-visit policy for all CDMX prisons (a sexual-orientation policy, not trans placement). No trans-specific custody unit, court ruling on housing, or documented placement case for CDMX was located; the country:MEX record reports the same absence. Adds: 1 verified (thin).
